input.title: Container architecture: Algo Insight package boundaries
input.description: Question: how does Prediction publish its candidate v3 package using Bricks, and how does Engine admit its separate local pilot v3 package? Non-candidate publication needs a verified promotion record; Engine profile admission is pilot-only. Two proven flows surround an unknown transfer/byte-equality/provenance gap. Solid arrows are current calls/data/control; the dotted package-to-package arrow is unresolved, never a live handoff. Top-to-bottom placement guides reading, not execution order. Model alternative details are in the Engine companion. Frozen source synthesis, not a runtime or deployment observation.

nodes.label: Role-separated research data

technical.responsibility: Binds separate selection and evaluation datasets by identity.

nodes.body: Prediction exports one shared research manifest with role datasets. Campaign composition binds selection to calibration and the separate evaluation role to final evaluation, rejecting path, revision, cutoff or ordered-column mismatches.

nodes.label: Prediction calibration

technical.responsibility: Owns preflight, candidate search and selected config publication.

nodes.body: Prediction owns the moex-prediction algorithmic campaign and algo-signals-calibrate command. Preflight checks source/input/provider identities; candidate search and calibration execute installed Bricks rule mechanics. The optimized SMA path imports private rule symbols, whose supported-public-interface status is not established.

nodes.label: Bricks AlgoSignals

technical.responsibility: Validates rule configs and computes signals in-process.

nodes.body: The installed algo-signals library owns typed rule configuration, stream/batch mechanics and versioned signal/config contracts. Calibration orchestration, economic evaluation, strategy sizing and execution belong to its consumers; Prediction also has a private SMA batch coupling.

nodes.label: Prediction evaluation/package

technical.responsibility: Verifies candidate identity and packages offline research results.

nodes.body: Final evaluation separately calls the installed Bricks public stream after candidate/build/symbol/cadence/market checks, applies the fixed one-bar-delay long/flat policy and publishes the canonical run. Packaging requires package/config status equality: this unpromoted campaign remains candidate; non-candidate publication needs an exact verified promotion record. The terminal receipt is offline and invokes no Engine.

nodes.label: Prediction v3 package

technical.responsibility: Publishes candidate config and verified offline evaluation evidence.

nodes.body: This producer-output identity is the candidate moex-prediction/strategy-package/v3 emitted by the unpromoted Prediction campaign: calibration fixes candidate status and the campaign supplies no promotion record. Package status must equal evaluated config status; a non-candidate package separately requires a verified promotion record for the exact config bytes, while candidate forbids one. No run or receipt links this output to Engine’s separate pilot package; offline completion does not imply Engine admission or quality approval.

nodes.label: Engine-local v3 package

technical.responsibility: Supplies tracked pilot package and config to Engine admission.

nodes.body: Engine independently tracks conf/strategies/dev/sber-sma-1-2/strategy-package.json and signal-config.yaml for its SBER/M5 pilot. Its README declares historical Prediction origin, but that declaration does not establish transfer, byte equality or run provenance from a package produced by this task’s frozen Prediction revision. The technical pilot is not a profitability claim.

nodes.label: Engine profile v9

technical.responsibility: Selects the local strategy and Engine-owned sizing policy.

nodes.body: The current dev profile points artifact_root to conf/strategies/dev and selects the SBER ticker’s algorithmic pilot package, target quantity and risk ceiling. A ticker selects exactly one algorithmic or contracted-model strategy family; this view’s primary instance is algorithmic.

nodes.label: Engine delivery admission

technical.responsibility: Checks local delivery and runtime identity before effects.

nodes.body: Profile/path/file checks and static family dispatch admit every ticker delivery before secrets and transports; profile lifecycle admission is pilot-only and rejects candidate. Algorithmic admission checks exact package/config/installed-rule identities, accepts declared SHA fields and reads config bytes without digest comparison. ValidatedStrategyPackage retains semantic fields and raw config bytes, not declared digests; evaluation files are checked as locators and are not read for launch.

nodes.label: Engine trade serve

technical.responsibility: Runs admitted signals through the continuous trade loop.

nodes.body: trade serve loads the profile with delivery checks, builds the service and runs it. The event loop processes tickers sequentially; TradeService.trade_once is an internal observation/decision/optional-submit step, not a public run-once command. Algorithmic warmup, neutral readiness and provider/invalid failures remain distinct.

nodes.label: Engine Account / Orders

technical.responsibility: Owns target sizing, decisions and optional order effects.

nodes.body: Both ready-signal families reach Engine’s shared decision path: NEUTRAL means NoTrade, LONG selects the configured target and SHORT selects zero. Account/OrderSubmitter preserve decision, pending/order progress and service failures; source inspection does not claim an order was submitted.

input.title: AlgoInsight: three-repository architecture overview
input.description: Which repository owns each boundary? Arrows point from consumer to dependency, not time or network calls. Static source review; brokers, news and deployment are outside this view.

nodes.label: Engine runtime

technical.responsibility: Composes market inputs, strategies and account execution.

nodes.body: The engine repository owns the continuous account service and broker-neutral planning/risk/accounting kernels. Its composition root selects concrete integrations; a package boundary is an in-process import boundary, not a service. Broker connectivity, the separate read-only P&L application and deployment details are outside this view.

nodes.label: MOEX integration

technical.responsibility: Admits completed bars from the shared Bricks client.

nodes.body: The MOEX adapter translates typed vendor rows into neutral market inputs and owns local readiness. Bricks owns live HTTPS, schema and pagination; local admission does not prove provider finality. Engine composition creates one client per named connection and closes it after source polls stop.

nodes.label: Signal integrations

technical.responsibility: Translate installed rule or model outcomes into neutral signals.

nodes.body: Static composition admits either an installed AlgoSignals strategy or a contracted Prediction model delivery. The model route reads completed M5 bars; invalid delivery stops composition. These adapters do not own account sizing, execution risk or the model policy.

nodes.label: Bricks market data

technical.responsibility: Owns typed market-data IO, schemas and provider mechanics.

nodes.body: algo-marketdata supplies the shared sync/async MOEX source, typed data contracts and local storage helpers. It handles native ISS intervals and M5 AlgoPack tradestats without claiming provider finality. Research feature/target semantics and trading admission remain with consumers.

nodes.label: Bricks signal rules

technical.responsibility: Turn candle and context inputs into versioned signal outcomes.

nodes.body: algo-signals owns reusable rule semantics and the public stream/outcome boundary. It neither acquires market data nor owns strategy decisions, portfolio state, final risk or order execution. Engine and Prediction consume it through explicit adapters rather than copying rules.

nodes.label: Prediction research/runtime

technical.responsibility: Builds research artifacts and exposes contracted model inference.

nodes.body: One moex-prediction distribution contains ML research, the algorithmic application, strategy policies and offline backtest namespaces; these are not separate services. Engine imports its contracted inference/artifact surface, not a remote research service. Prediction uses installed Bricks rules and data helpers; it does not own broker submit or production risk.

input.title: AlgoInsight: three-repository architecture overview
input.description: Which repository owns each boundary? Arrows point from consumer to dependency, not time or network calls. Static source review; brokers, news and deployment are outside this view.

nodes.label: Engine runtime

technical.responsibility: Composes market inputs, strategies and account execution.

nodes.body: The engine repository owns the continuous account service and broker-neutral planning/risk/accounting kernels. Its composition root selects concrete integrations; a package boundary is an in-process import boundary, not a service. Broker connectivity, the separate read-only P&L application and deployment details are outside this view.

nodes.label: MOEX integration

technical.responsibility: Admits completed bars from the shared Bricks client.

nodes.body: The MOEX adapter translates typed vendor rows into neutral market inputs and owns local readiness. Bricks owns live HTTPS, schema and pagination; local admission does not prove provider finality. Engine composition creates one client per named connection and closes it after source polls stop.

nodes.label: Signal integrations

technical.responsibility: Translate installed rule or model outcomes into neutral signals.

nodes.body: Static composition admits either an installed AlgoSignals strategy or a contracted Prediction model delivery. The model route reads completed M5 bars; invalid delivery stops composition. These adapters do not own account sizing, execution risk or the model policy.

nodes.label: Bricks market data

technical.responsibility: Owns typed market-data IO, schemas and provider mechanics.

nodes.body: algo-marketdata supplies the shared sync/async MOEX source, typed data contracts and local storage helpers. It handles native ISS intervals and M5 AlgoPack tradestats without claiming provider finality. Research feature/target semantics and trading admission remain with consumers.

nodes.label: Bricks signal rules

technical.responsibility: Turn candle and context inputs into versioned signal outcomes.

nodes.body: algo-signals owns reusable rule semantics and the public stream/outcome boundary. It neither acquires market data nor owns strategy decisions, portfolio state, final risk or order execution. Engine and Prediction consume it through explicit adapters rather than copying rules.

nodes.label: Prediction research/runtime

technical.responsibility: Builds research artifacts and exposes contracted model inference.

nodes.body: One moex-prediction distribution contains ML research, the algorithmic application, strategy policies and offline backtest namespaces; these are not separate services. Engine imports its contracted inference/artifact surface, not a remote research service. Prediction uses installed Bricks rules and data helpers; it does not own broker submit or production risk.
